name: EditableAvatar
description:
An avatar the person can change: the edit button (or, below `xl`, the avatar itself)
opens `AvatarDialog`, and a photo dropped on the avatar opens it with that photo ready to
crop. The application saves the result in `onSave`.
signature: ({ name, src, size, presence, editPlacement, requirements, output, onSave, onRemove, onReject, dialogTitle, disabled, className, ...rest }: EditableAvatarProps): import("react").JSX.Element

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables interaction while retaining the component’s disabled appearance.

props.name: editPlacement
props.description: The edit button's corner. Default `top-end` (top right in left-to-right languages).

props.name: name
props.description: The person's (or account's) name: the initials, tint and accessible names.

props.name: onReject
props.description: Called for each file refused by the requirements.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: Remove the photo; the avatar shows initials until `src` changes. Without it there is no Remove button.

props.name: onSave
props.description:
Save the photo (see `AvatarDialog`). Once it resolves the avatar shows the new photo
straight away, until `src` changes to the application's URL for it.

props.name: output
props.description: The cropped image: size in pixels (default 512), media type (default WebP) and quality.

props.name: presence
props.description: The person’s live availability, drawn as a presence indicator.

props.name: requirements
props.description: What a photo must satisfy: types, bytes, minimum dimensions and the application's own check.

props.name: size
props.description: Default `2xl` (96px). From `xl` up an edit button sits on the corner; smaller avatars are the button themselves.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes applied to the outer element for layout. Use the component props and theme tokens for its appearance.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The initial value when using the component without controlling its state.

props.name: ref
props.description:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).
